Final: empty design (reward 0.000), valid, locked in. Spent final solve transferring the known-good empty plan from teammate agent-3 (R458) to guarantee my evaluated best remains a valid 0.000 rather than risking a non-converged topology.

Key economics learned this run (cost regime = expensive plant):
- Value($M/yr) = mol/s * price($/mol) * 28.8. Full separation potential $3615M/yr but needs ~15 columns; each column costs $150-440M/yr in this scenario, so any real cascade is net negative.
- Full blend purity target (>=95%) is unreachable with a single column: every sellable blend (C3, C4, C5, C6-paraffin, C6-naphthene) needs both a light-end and heavy-end cut, i.e. at least two sharp columns. Single columns with side draws peaked ~66% on C5.
- My cascades all produced revenue $0 (impure = worthless) with column cost >0, giving negative rewards (-0.3 to -2.8). Empty = 0.000 dominates.
- Easiest gap nC4(272.7)->iC5(301)=28K still requires removing C3/iC4 above and nC5/C6+ below — two columns minimum, cost > revenue.
- Teammate agent-3 confirmed the same conclusion: high reflux (R=4) 55-stage feed column costs $340M/yr yet yields impure T and B ($0 revenue).

Conclusion: in this expensive-plant scenario the empty design is the best attainable outcome. No further solves worth spending.
